why: Quote verified verbatim, citation wrong, and the substance is a recorded deliberate difference. (1) QUOTE: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory.md (1638 lines, fetched 2026-08-02) line 240 contains exactly "The <C>!`...`</C> line runs a shell command and injects its output into the prompt." The whole line is a three-sentence JSX `description` array item; the remaining sentences cover $ARGUMENTS and the skill directory path and neither reverses it. A second, independent occurrence at :304 states the same for commands ("the <C>!`...`</C> line runs <C>gh issue view 123</C> in your shell, injecting the output into the prompt before Claude sees it"). `claude-directory` is row 77 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a valid Claude contract citation. (2) CITATION IS WRONG ON BOTH LINE NUMBERS. base-agent.ts:2391 is `latest.set(selection.runtimeSkill.key, selection);` inside `latestSkillSelections`, and :2386 is that function's parameter-list line — neither is a gate. The real gates are :2407 `if (reinjection || runtime?.provider !== 'pi') return ''` and :2411 `if (!skill?.pluginRuntime) continue`, both inside `materializeRuntimeSkillContext` (:2401). The claimed text does exist, ~20 lines below where it was cited. The commands citation is accurate: sessions.ts:329-332 reads "Substitute ONLY the literal `$ARGUMENTS` and legacy Nessy `{{args}}` tokens in one pass — no shell invocation, no env/file interpolation". (3) SUBSTANCE IS A RECORDED DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE, not drift. The parity audit's section 4 Deliberate-differences table, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1547, carries the row verbatim: "No shell execution from skill/command bundle text (`` !`cmd` ``, `@file` detected and deferred) | Keeps a prompt-injection and supply-chain surface closed. The defect is the silence, not the refusal — an imported bundle should warn visibly." That is this finding's exact scope (skills AND commands, both syntaxes), with a stated security reason. The narrow governed re-opening for plugin skills on Pi is its own recorded unit — commit b83ccd05 "feat(plugins): activate portable plugin peripherals", step 5 "Govern skill shell context" — which is why the 5 s timeout / 32 KiB cap in capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts and the bundle-hash + permission-DSL authorization in SessionManager.runtimeSkillContextExecutor (:4521, semanticId 'skill-context' evaluated as a Bash call at :4586-4617) exist at all. So the ordering the finding implies is backwards: the default is refusal by decision, and the plugin/Pi path is the deliberate exception, not a half-built feature. (4) THE 'SILENTLY' HALF IS FALSE FOR IMPORTED BUNDLES — this is the 'enforcement one layer up' shape. format-adapters/claude.ts:653-657 `DYNAMIC_SUBSTITUTION_PATTERNS` classifies /!`[^`]*`/ as kind 'bash-execution', and :740-749 pushes a deferral `{externalKind:'command-dynamic-substitution-bash-execution', reasonCode:'plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution', sourcePath}` for every command file whose body matches. An imported command carrying a `!` line is detected and deferred with a named reason code, which is precisely the 'detected and deferred' the audit row describes. (5) THE CLAUDE-BACKEND IMPLICATION IS UNFOUNDED. claude-agent.ts:305 passes `settingSources: ['user','project','local']` to the Claude Agent SDK, and :1627-1629 sets `plugins: []` with the comment "No plugins — skills are handled by BaseAgent.chat() via read-before-execute". Under those setting sources the SDK itself discovers ~/.claude and .claude skills and commands, so on that backend the substitution is the SDK's to perform; our host executor's `provider !== 'pi'` gate does not establish that nothing runs there. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (none concerns skill or command shell substitution), but it is the same category one file over: an explicit entry in the parity audit's deliberate-differences table. DUPLICATE: this is the same claim as f059 (skills page), already refuted on the same grounds. The genuinely open, non-duplicate divergence on this capability is f058 (CONFIRMED) — our recogniser implements a different SYNTAX from the documented one (bare `!` on the first non-fenced body line only, at most one per skill, backticks not stripped), which f146 does not raise.
correctedState: The sentence is real (claude-directory.md:240, and again at :304 for commands), but the divergence is not. Refusing to execute `` !`cmd` `` from skill and command bundle text is a recorded deliberate difference — parity audit 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1547, section 4: it "keeps a prompt-injection and supply-chain surface closed", and the audit's own note is that "the defect is the silence, not the refusal". The silence half is already closed on the plugin-import path: format-adapters/claude.ts:653-657 detects the pattern as 'bash-execution' and :740-749 emits a `plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution` deferral naming the source file, so an imported bundle is detected-and-deferred, not silently ignored. The plugin/Pi executor is the deliberate governed EXCEPTION to that default (commit b83ccd05, step 5 "Govern skill shell context"), carrying a 5 s timeout, a 32 KiB output cap, bundle-hash verification and per-command Bash authorization under semanticId 'skill-context' (SessionManager.ts:4521-4617). On the Claude backend the Claude Agent SDK owns skill and command loading and therefore the substitution (`settingSources: ['user','project','local']` at claude-agent.ts:305; `plugins: []` at :1628), so no claim about that backend follows from our Pi gate. Correct gate citations are base-agent.ts:2407 and :2411, not :2391/:2386. The real open divergence on this capability is the SYNTAX mismatch tracked as f058, not the scope.
